verdicts.summary: The note's failure mode (an alive but unresponsive managed server blocks every reconnect until a runner change or an explicit disconnect) is what finding 0 reports. The stderr message does reach the caller, so the visible_effect claim holds.

I could not push any path past the outer timeout. Each wait is bounded by its deadline plus at most one 1s probe. The worst realistic paths add up to about 64-68s, below the 90s node-script bound, and the archive bound is 900s.
evidence: packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:304-349 (wait_ready loop checks the deadline and each probe is capped at 1s)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:676,706,714-716,720,744 (the longest chain is a 2s adopt probe, a 2s reuse probe or kill-wait, then a 60s wait)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:917-919 (outer timeout chosen by runner type)

verdicts.summary: The only hazard is the gap between tunnels.delete and closeTunnelEntry, which finding 1 reports. The remote-stop semantics are correct. The finalizer's stopRemote check is the only place that relies on map identity, and disconnect still runs the stop script even when the map has no entry.
evidence: packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:1401-1409 (the manager-scope finalizer closes only entries still in the map)

verdicts.summary: A recycled PID turns the new 'wait then exit 1' branch into a stuck state with no server behind it. After a remote reboot or crash the stale PID file can name an unrelated live process, so every reconnect fails after 60s.
verdicts.scenario: 1. A managed server is launched and ~/.t3/ssh-launch/<key>/pid, port and managed (= managed) are written. 2. The remote host reboots or the server crashes, and the PID file survives. 3. An unrelated process gets the same PID. 4. The user reconnects. server_running passes because kill -0 succeeds and the process is not a zombie. 5. Nothing listens on REMOTE_PORT, so wait_ready runs the full 60s and the script exits 1. 6. The script never reaches pick_port or relaunch. Each retry repeats the 60s wait. The only exits are a runner change or an explicit disconnect, and the stop script then kills that unrelated PID (line 780-781). If the default runtime file also names that PID, the branch at line 671 is taken and ends in the same place.
verdicts.consequence: After a remote reboot, reconnect can hang about 60s and fail on every attempt, with the message 'server is still running but did not become ready', although no T3 server exists. Previously the 2s probe failed and a new server was launched, though it also killed the unrelated PID. Recovery now needs a manual disconnect, which kills the unrelated process.
evidence: packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:625-630 (server_running checks only kill -0 and the zombie state, not process identity)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:657-659 (state read from the persistent PID, port and managed files)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:711-723 (alive PID, wait_ready fails, exit 1 with no relaunch)
packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:780-781 (stop script kills the recorded PID)
